recognize_zh: 周邊血抹片中可見三顆小至中型母細胞，核質比極高、染色質細緻、細胞質只剩一圈嗜鹼性邊緣且無顆粒，同視野沒有嗜中性球，提示循環中的淋巴母細胞。
features: Three circulating blasts, small to intermediate in size (about 1.5-2x a red cell)
Very high N:C ratio with only a thin rim of basophilic agranular cytoplasm
Round to slightly irregular nuclei with fine, evenly dispersed chromatin; nucleoli not conspicuous
No Auer rods or cytoplasmic granules
Red cells largely normochromic without significant poikilocytosis; no neutrophils or platelets clearly seen in this field
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows scattered circulating blasts that are small to intermediate in size with a very high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio, finely dispersed chromatin, inconspicuous nucleoli and a scant rim of agranular basophilic cytoplasm. No Auer rods are identified. Red cells show no significant morphologic abnormality, and no neutrophils are present in this field. The blasts are morphologically consistent with lymphoblasts; flow cytometry is required for lineage assignment and, in this case, supports B-lymphoblastic leukemia.

ddx.vs: Reactive lymphocytes have more abundant cytoplasm that scallops around red cells and condensed rather than fine blastic chromatin.
Myeloblasts often show more cytoplasm, visible nucleoli, granules or Auer rods, but agranular forms require flow cytometry to separate.
CLL cells have coarse, clumped 'soccer-ball' chromatin and are accompanied by smudge cells rather than fine blastic chromatin.
